children.text: The Cultural Center of the Philippines (CCP) complex stands on land reclaimed from Manila Bay, bringing together National Artist Leandro Locsin's theater and convention center, the Coconut Palace and the Star City amusement park. The Main Building is under renovation ahead of its reopening, but black box theater shows and seaside sunsets can be enjoyed right now.

The CCP Complex is the campus of the Cultural Center of the Philippines, built on land reclaimed from Manila Bay west of Roxas Boulevard, where the southern tip of the City of Manila meets Pasay City. Around the CCP Main Building (Tanghalang Pambansa), the heart of Philippine performing arts, large landmarks such as the PICC convention center, the Coconut Palace, the Folk Arts Theater and the Manila Film Center, along with the Star City amusement park and a seafood dining strip, are spread out between wide lawns and the sea.
The complex began in
, when a presidential executive order created the cultural center. Then–First Lady Imelda Marcos led the project, and the Main Building opened as the Theater of Performing Arts on
September 8, 1969
. Next came the Folk Arts Theater, built in just
77 days
for the Miss Universe pageant in
; the PICC, which opened in
for the IMF–World Bank annual meetings; the Coconut Palace, built in
; and the Manila Film Center, built for the first Manila International Film Festival in
. The Main Building, the PICC and the Folk Arts Theater were all designed by National Artist Leandro V. Locsin.
Locsin's architecture is often summed up as the "floating volume." The Main Building echoes the traditional Filipino bahay kubo house: a huge two-story, travertine-clad box hovers
above the ground on concave concrete supports. Crushed seashells were mixed into the concrete for texture, and an octagonal pool with fountains sits in front. In
, the PICC and the artworks inside and around it were jointly declared a National Cultural Treasure.
Be aware that much of the complex is under construction. The CCP Main Building has been closed since
for seismic retrofitting and façade replacement and aims to reopen in
early 2027
; until then you can only see it from outside. Meanwhile, plays and dance continue at the black box theater, which opened in
; the Coconut Palace finished its restoration in
August 2026
; and the PICC reopened in
September 2025
after renovations. The complex suits travelers interested in architecture and modern history, long-stay visitors who want to see local performances, and families looking for an amusement park.

blocks.title: CCP Main Building and octagonal pool

children.text: Considered Locsin's masterpiece, the Main Building can still be viewed from outside during construction, from the plaza on the Roxas Boulevard side and by the pool. Once it reopens, the 1,815-seat main theater (Tanghalang Nicanor Abelardo), the little theater, the studio theater and the arthouse cinema will open again, and you will again be able to see the lobby's spiral staircase and its three capiz-shell chandeliers representing Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao.
This theater became the center of CCP performances while the Main Building is closed. It opened on
September 8, 2022

, the CCP's anniversary, and its seating can be reconfigured to suit the stage, holding 272–320 people. It hosts plays by resident company Tanghalang Pilipino and the new-play festival Virgin Labfest, and tickets for
shows cost about

This guesthouse was designed by National Artist Francisco Mañosa, and about 70% of its materials are coconut wood and shells. It is famous for its octagonal plan, a roof shaped like the traditional salakot hat, a chandelier made of 101 coconut shells, and a dining table inlaid with 40,000 pieces of shell. In
it was offered to Pope John Paul II as his lodging, but he reportedly turned it down as too lavish.
Opened in

as Asia's first international convention center, this long, horizontal concrete building is another Locsin masterpiece. Only event attendees can go inside, so most visitors view the exterior and the APEC Sculpture Garden with its 20 sculptures from outside, and see Arturo Luz's sculpture Anito in the courtyard and the lobby artworks through the virtual tour on the official website.
This amusement park sits deep inside the complex. Its signature rides are the Giant Star Wheel, the Philippines' tallest Ferris wheel at
with 32 gondolas; the Star Flyer, the country's only inverted roller coaster; and Snow World, with its artificial snow slide. It opens Thursday and Friday
and Saturday and Sunday
, and is closed Monday to Wednesday.

blocks.title: Folk Arts Theater and Manila Film Center

children.text: The 8,458-seat Folk Arts Theater is known for its huge roof spanning
between columns with no supports in between. The Manila Film Center, lined with massive columns, was rushed to completion for a film festival in
, and an accident that killed workers during construction has made it the subject of many ghost stories. Both are closed for safety reasons and can only be seen from outside.

The west side of the complex meets the sea, so you can watch the sun set over Manila Bay up close. The breakwater by Harbour Square, where yachts are moored, and the shore in front of Seascape Village are favorite sunset spots, and after dark the illuminated Star City Ferris wheel adds to the night view. For the bayside promenade and sunset cruises, see the
Manila Bay
entry as well.
The CCP is home to Pasinaya (
February
), the country's largest multi-arts festival, and the independent film festival Cinemalaya (
August

). Pasinaya works on a pay-what-you-can, watch-all-you-can basis, so you can see several performances in one day. During the renovation, they are being held at other venues, so check that year's location.
Get off at LRT Line 1 Vito Cruz Station and walk about
20 minutes
west, or take a Grab, to the plaza in front of the CCP Main Building.
See the Main Building's exterior and octagonal pool, then cross the south lawn toward the black box theater and the Star City entrance.
View the Folk Arts Theater and the Coconut Palace from outside. If the Coconut Palace is open for public visits, go inside.
See the PICC exterior and the APEC Sculpture Garden, then walk west to the colonnade of the Manila Film Center.
Head to the shore by Harbour Square and watch the sun set over Manila Bay.
At Seascape Village, pick your seafood and have it cooked for dinner, then take a Grab back.

There is little shade in the complex, and the buildings are farther apart than they look. Start in the late afternoon, and check ahead, because roads around the PICC are blocked on days when international meetings are held.

children.text: Have lunch at Seascape Village or Harbour Square.
Enter Star City when it opens, at
on Saturday and Sunday or
on Thursday and Friday, and ride the Star Flyer and the Giant Star Wheel first.
Cool off at Snow World and enjoy family rides such as the double-decker carousel.
Leave Star City and walk to the shore to watch the sunset.
Have dinner at Seascape Village.
Catch an evening show at the black box theater.

Star City is closed Monday to Wednesday, and individual rides have maintenance days, so check the official announcements before you go. Show start times at the black box theater vary by production, so confirm them when buying tickets.
LRT Line 1's Vito Cruz Station is the closest. A single ride costs about
, depending on distance and card type.
From the station, head west along Vito Cruz Street (now officially Pablo Ocampo Street) and cross Roxas Boulevard to reach the north side of the complex, in front of the Main Building. It is about
1.5km
, roughly a
20-minute
walk, so at midday or at night it is better to take a Grab from the station.
Take a jeepney running along Taft Avenue and get off at the Vito Cruz intersection, the same spot as the LRT station. The minimum fare is
for traditional jeepneys and
for modern ones.
These jeepney fares took effect on
September 28, 2026
and may change again. After getting off, walk west as you would from the LRT.
From Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), a Grab takes about
20–40 minutes
and costs about
. From Makati it takes about
15–30 minutes
, and longer at rush hour or in the rain.
The complex is large, and entering just "CCP" may drop you at the wrong gate. Set your destination to the building you want, such as Tanghalang Ignacio Gimenez, Star City, Coconut Palace or PICC.
From the Main Building it is about
to Star City, about
to the PICC and about
to the Coconut Palace, all within walking distance. There is almost no shade, though, and many wide roads, so use the crosswalks.
The
December–April
dry season is the best time to walk around. Average daily highs in Manila's Port Area are about
in
January
and about
in
April
, with only 3–4 rainy days a month. From
March to May
, however, the shadeless complex gets very hot at midday, so move around in the late afternoon.
June–November
is the rainy season. In
July–August
it rains about 19 days a month, and when typhoons pass, the seaside promenade becomes dangerous and Star City's outdoor rides stop. On rainy days, plan around indoor performances.

and may vary depending on local conditions.
There are few places to stay inside the complex. The Sofitel Philippine Plaza, long its signature hotel, closed in
July 2024
; today a resort-style hotel next to Seascape Village operates at about
a night. Most visitors stay in Malate or Ermita, about
10 minutes
away by car, around SM Mall of Asia to the south, or in Makati, and come and go by Grab.

For food, Seascape Village on the complex's western shore is the main draw. It is a paluto dining strip: buy shrimp, crab and fish by weight at the seafood market, then hand them to a neighboring restaurant to cook the way you like. Shrimp or crab costs about
per 0.5kg, and a cooked dish about
. Most places open around
and stay open until about
11 PM–midnight

. Harbour Square, by the yacht marina, has a cluster of bay-view restaurants, but some have closed, so check before you go. Outside food is not allowed in Star City except baby milk and baby food, so you will need to use the food stalls inside.

While the Main Building is closed, CCP performances are split among the black box theater, the Metropolitan Theater, the Samsung Performing Arts Theater in Makati, the PICC and other venues. Always check the venue address before buying tickets.
Star City tickets are sold only on the official website and at the ticket booth, and online tickets can be used within
30 days
of purchase. PWD and senior citizen discounts are available only at the ticket booth.
Star City rents out wheelchairs and strollers for
an hour, and there is a promotion giving a free Star Pass to a birthday celebrant who comes with four paying companions. Terms may change.
The Coconut Palace reopened on
August 25, 2026
, but it is also used as a venue for international meetings, so check announcements from its owner, the GSIS (Government Service Insurance System), for public visiting schedules and fees.
The PICC has no public tours, so see the interior during events open to everyone, such as trade fairs.
To watch the sunset, find your spot by the shore at least
30 minutes
before the sun goes down.

News on the Main Building's reopening and performance schedules appears first on the CCP's official website and social media. Season performances by resident companies such as Ballet Philippines and the Philippine Philharmonic Orchestra are also announced there.

The complex's buildings are symbols of large projects under the Marcos regime, and opinions on them are divided. Knowing the background, such as the coconut industry levy that went into the Coconut Palace, gives the architecture more depth.
The CCP Main Building (Tanghalang Pambansa) has been closed for construction since
and aims to reopen in
early 2027
, but the schedule may slip. Check official CCP announcements before you visit.
When large international meetings such as summits are held at the PICC, roads around the complex are closed and Star City also closes temporarily. For the ASEAN Summit, Star City set
November 7–18, 2026
as a temporary closure period.
The lease on Star City's land ends in
, and the government is pursuing a sale of the site, so operations may change. Check the official website to confirm it is open before you go.
The Folk Arts Theater and the Manila Film Center are closed due to structural damage. Do not go inside the fences.
At night, apart from areas around event venues, the complex has many deserted, dark roads. Do not walk around late; call a Grab instead.
Paluto at Seascape Village charges separately for the seafood by weight and for the cooking. Before ordering, check the scale reading, the price per kg and the cooking fee.
During typhoons, high waves hit the breakwater and the seaside promenade. Stay away from the shore when warnings are issued.
